messages:
Maya: Heads-up: observed persistent GPU RSS growth on long-context chat runs when we do a kernel switch mid-request for mistral-7b (MQA). Repro with streaming where system+user turns keep appending.

Maya: Minimal repro: run streaming decode forcing switch after ~2k tokens. It reliably creeps up until eviction thrashes.
```bash
python tools/repro_longprefix.py --model mistral-7b-mqa --switch-after 2048 --ctx 8192 --batch 1
```

Maya: Quick profiling shows repeated allocs at the same kv_arena offsets even after frees: allocator logs show free at X then alloc at same X but with mismatched size/alignment later.

Maya: Example allocator trace (sanitized):
```
alloc: kv_arena+0x1f4000 size=0x6000
free:  kv_arena+0x1f4000
alloc: kv_arena+0x1f4000 size=0x5000   # later, unexpected reuse pattern
```

Maya: Hypothesis: kernel A (low-latency FP) and kernel B (quantized/fast-path) use different slice packing / write-mask alignment. When we switch, the allocator metadata ends up inconsistent (header flags/padding) so freed runs are not coalesced or not visible to the free-list used by the other kernel.

Devin: Could rope-scaling (positional multiplier adjustments) move write boundaries enough to cause different slice offsets? Mistral's ropemul for long ctxs is funky.

Maya: Yes, rope scaling will shift where token-key/value pairs are written, which interacts with slice-size math. But the core issue looks like padding vs. block size mismatch in the free/coalesce path.

Frank: Do we see this on Qwen or Llama variants or just MQA builds?

Maya: Reprobed on qwen-7b in quantized mode and saw a milder version, but Llama FP paths didn't show the leak. Pattern: MQA/packed kernels show the strongest symptom.

Lia: Two likely root causes: 1) allocator header flagging not atomically updated across kernel-switch path (race when two decoders touch same GTID), 2) different kernels expect different granularity for free-list entries (16B vs 8B packing), leaving micro-fragments that never get coalesced.

Devin: Can you reproduce faster with parallel streams hitting the same model-state? If it's a header race, parallelism should escalate fails.

Maya: Yes — adding --parallel 2 speeds it up and increases alloc churn. I'll attach a small heapdump and perf snippet.

perf-bot: Uploaded artifacts: artifacts/1807512345/kv-repro-perf.flame.gz and artifacts/1807512345/heapdump.txt

Maya: Heapdump excerpt:
```
free-list: [0x1f0000(size=0x2000), 0x1f2000(size=0x2000)]
alloc seen: 0x1f0000 size=0x1800
alloc seen: 0x1f0000 size=0x2000  # allocator returned same base with different bookkeeping
```

Frank: That looks like coalesce didn't run or header got corrupted. Maybe kernels use different magic bytes in page headers for validation. If kernel B sees a header it doesn't recognize, it won't re-add to coalesce list.

Lia: Mitigation: force kernel affinity during a request. We already have --disable-kernel-switch flag; enabling that prevents the leak in smoke. Can we add it to the long-prefix canary while we fix allocator invariants?

Frank: I added a nightly canary job case: long-prefix 8k, parallel=2, tolerate 1 failure before alert. If we see regression post-patch, we'll know.

Maya: Drafting a PR: two parts — defensive coalesce-on-free (idempotent), and an assert that validates header magic across kernel types when freeing. Also add unit tests for mixed alignment free/alloc patterns.

Devin: For the unit tests, enumerate alignments [8,16,32], and simulate mixed MQA/non-MQA packing. Add a tight parallel allocator test (threads=2) to stress header races.

Lia: Also add a tiny integration test that runs the repro for 30s under ASAN/UBSAN in CI to catch memory header corruption early.

Maya: Filed INF-1428 with logs and repro (https://rwi/issue/INF-1428). PR draft will land this afternoon.

Frank: One more note: check the eviction code path. It currently picks a free candidate by exact-size match in the free-bins. If fragmentation leaves many small runs, eviction can fail to reclaim even though total free sum is high. Consider adding a fallback to search adjacent bins for coalescing before OOM.

Maya: Good call. I'll add a fallback that attempts a coalesce scan over neighbouring bins before giving up. That should blunt the immediate OOMs.

Devin: If we change coalesce behaviour, ensure we don't regress latency by adding heavy scans on the hot path. Make scans capped (max 8 checks).

Lia: Assigning owners: eng-runtime/Maya = fix, reviewers Frank+Devin. Can someone add a perf canary for qwen-quant too? If packing differences differ, we want early coverage.

Frank: Will add qwen-quant long-prefix to canary matrix.

Maya: ETA: PR draft today, unit tests tomorrow, canary coverage by end of week.

Lia: :thumbsup: Keep notes here if you find model-specific packing tables. If this touches MQA packing constants we might need a small model-metadata bump for kernel compatibility checks.

Maya: Will do. Thanks all.
